sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13:7, 58 pp.
sources.note: No chapter on Attapady/Palu Kurumba (covers Muduga, Betta Kurumba, Mullu Kurumba etc.); irrelevant for this language.

sources.citation: Abraham, Binny. 2020. Centralised vowels in Dravidian languages of Attappady: acoustic, historical and orthographic perspectives. PhD thesis, Central University of Kerala. 162 pp.
sources.note: Nothing for Pālu Kuṟumba (the phonology chapters are on Muḍuga; Pālu Kuṟumba appears in the literature review §1.6.3.2 and the orthography chapter 5). Useful for bibliography: cites Lathikakumari 1977 'Phonology of the Kurumba language of Attappady' (Univ. Kerala) and Kapp 1978.

sources.citation: Sampreetha K. [c.2017]. Biodiversity maintenance and shift in the language of Attappady Kurumpa: socio-cognitive linguistic approach. PhD thesis (in Malayalam), Dept. of Malayalam, University of Madras. Shodhganga 10603/293971.
sources.note: Nothing; §3.9.16 'Kurumba bhasha' (p.106) is a sociolinguistic paragraph (mixed Tamil-Malayalam-Kannada character, no script); thesis is lexical-ecological, no phonology.

sources.citation: Syam, S.K., P.N. Ravindran & C.G. Syama (with K.S. Pradeep Kumar, Mini P.V.). 2017. Descriptive Grammar of Muduga and Kurumba Languages. Kozhikode: KIRTADS. 318 pp. (= Glottolog 'Ravindran, Syama & Syam 2017')
sources.note: Nothing. Part II (Kurumba, pp.107-308) Ch. II 'Phoneme identification' (pp.124-151) gives a 5-vowel/24-consonant inventory with positional distributions and clusters; no section or sentence on stress, accent or prosody (full-text grep of born-digital PDF and IA scanned: 'stress'/'accent' occur only in a generic textbook sentence about morphology on p.152 and a gloss 'accent').

sources.citation: Zvelebil, Kamil V. 1980. Jēnu Kuṟumba: first report on a tribal language of the Nilgiri area. BLS 6: 111-119.
sources.note: Different language (Jenu Kurumba); scanned and grepped because Abraham 2020 cites it for Pālu Kuṟumba vowels — no mention of Pālu Kuṟumba or of stress.

sources.citation: Rajendran, N. 1978. Description of the language of Mudugas. PhD thesis, Dept. of Linguistics, University of Kerala. Ch.7 'Comparison' (pp.462-499) compares Muduga with Attappady Kurumba (data from the 1977 Kerala MA dissertations of Geetha S. Nair, Lathikakumari, Vasanthakumari + author's field notes).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. §7.1.1.4 'Suprasegmentals' (p.471-472): 'No difference is observed in junctures and terminals. Two junctures and three terminals are available in both the languages. Four pitch levels are identified in Muduga while Kurumba has only three pitch levels.' Stress is not among the suprasegmentals posited for either language; Ch.1 §1.5 (Muduga) likewise lists only length, junctures, pitch levels, terminals, intonation.

sources.citation: Kapp, Dieter B. 2019. Pālu-Kuṟumba: Grammatik, Textproben und Wörterbuch. (Beiträge zur Kenntnis südasiatischer Sprachen und Literaturen 30.) Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz. ISBN 978-3-447-11244-4. See Teil I §1 'Phonetik und Phonologie', pp.14-16.

sources.note: The only modern linguist's grammar of Pālu Kuṟumba (Kapp's 1974-76 fieldwork); §1.2 'Beschreibung der Phoneme und Allophone' is the likeliest place for a Betonung remark; would supersede everything else.
